title: Stack dispatched terminals onto the largest non-focused terminal window
body:
Plan runs dispatch many workers into one Project. Today each dispatched terminal splits the FOCUSED window (`tile_new(id, prev_focus)` in `add_terminal_receiving`, src/wm.rs), and focus deliberately stays put, so the orchestrator pane halves on every dispatch (1/2, 1/4, 1/8...) - the "ratios can sink below 10%" gotcha in docs/tiling-tree.md. Fix: stack later workers as tabs instead of splitting.

DESIGN (decided; if you find it wrong, `kanban block` with the reason rather than switching silently):
- Scope: only `add_terminal_receiving` (the fire-and-watch path: `foreman open` via `add_terminal_cmd`, and `kanban dispatch`). Manual "new terminal" (`add_terminal`), layout Apply's fresh slots, and image/view windows keep today's placement.
- Target: the largest (by on-screen area) TILED window in this manager whose active tab is a Terminal, EXCLUDING the focused window. Floating, minimized, and the Sessions panel are never targets. Ties: earliest in tree order.
- If there is a target: append the new terminal as a tab on it. Keep the target's current front tab active (same as layout Apply stacking extras, docs/project-layouts.md) - a dispatch must never change what the user is looking at. Focus stays exactly where it was.
- If there is no target (e.g. only the orchestrator pane is open): place as today via `tile_new(id, prev_focus)`. So the first worker splits beside the orchestrator and every later worker stacks onto a worker window: orchestrator keeps 1/2.
- Do NOT reuse `merge_windows` as-is: it focuses the destination and activates the merged tab. Factor a non-focusing variant or push the tab directly; keep one home for the tab-append logic.
- No new setting.

TERMINAL IDS (checked 2026-10-20, not a blocker): a terminal's Member id lives on the Session (`term_id`, == FOREMAN_TERMINAL_ID), not on its window, because merge/untab/restore already move terminals between windows. send/snapshot/status (`resolve_terminal` -> `terminal_location`, "the sole seam"), close (`close_terminal`), chat delivery (`chat_tick`), hook events (`apply_hook_event`), kanban claims/orphans (`term_states`, dispatch undo) all resolve by term_id across every tab. Tests: `term_id_survives_untab`, `restored_tab_stack_gets_unique_term_ids`. Keep it that way: never look a terminal up by window id.
- TRAP in `add_terminal_receiving`: the chat join reads the new window back by window id (`self.windows.iter().find(|w| w.id == id)`) for the display name. Take the name before stacking (or from the tab), or the join is silently skipped in release builds.
- Add one test: a dispatched worker stacked as a NON-active tab still receives a targeted chat post, answers `snapshot`, and its card claim is not orphaned.

DONE WHEN:
- Pure, table-tested target choice (inputs: windows with rect, tiled/floating/minimized, active-tab kind, focused flag) separate from egui.
- wm tests: (1) with only a focused orchestrator, first dispatch tiles beside it; (2) second dispatch stacks onto the first worker's window, focus and that window's front tab unchanged, orchestrator rect unchanged; (3) with two candidate windows the larger one is chosen; (4) floating/minimized terminals and the focused window are never chosen.
- docs/tiling-tree.md "New windows tile by default" paragraph gains the dispatch-stacking rule and why (one short paragraph); update the ratio-floor gotcha if it no longer applies to dispatch.
- GUI claim: one inspected screenshot of an orchestrator plus 4 dispatched workers (ask the human to run the build-screenshot skill; do not drive the mouse).

Gate: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --target-dir target/agent; cargo test --target-dir target/agent. Follow foreman-architecture-contract (local vs screen rects, focus cascade) and foreman-validation-and-qa.
